label: Iraq Museum IM 77781
summary: Formerly unpublished Jewish Babylonian Aramaic incantation bowl given to the Iraq Museum and published by Ali Faraj.

source.title: Remarks on a New Aramaic Incantation Bowl IM 77781
source.citation: Faraj, Ali. ‘Remarks on a New Aramaic Incantation Bowl IM 77781.’ Journal of Semitic Studies 68.1 (2023): 89–95. doi:10.1093/jss/fgac026.

appearance.title: IM 77781
appearance.description: Editio princeps of a fifteen-line Jewish Babylonian Aramaic incantation protecting a client, his wife, and daughter against enemies' curses.

claims.value_text: Protection of the client, his wife, and his daughter against curses of enemies and opponents

events.details: Gift of Mr. Ismāʿīl Nāyf to the Iraq Museum.

label: British Museum 1957,0925.1
summary: Jewish Babylonian Aramaic bowl omitted from Segal (2000) after an earlier modern-copy assessment, but subsequently authenticated and published by Levene and Bohak (2012).

source.title: incantation bowl: 1957,0925.1
source.citation: The British Museum, Collections Online, ‘incantation bowl,’ registration 1957,0925.1 (accessed 2026-09-04).

appearance.title: incantation bowl
appearance.description: Complete ceramic bowl with a black-ink spiral inscription, initially considered a modern copy but now described by the museum as authentic.

claims.value_text: Diameter 21.20 cm; height 6.50 cm; rim thickness 0.50 cm
Originally considered a modern copy in 1958; British Museum curator's comments now state that the inscription's content establishes its authenticity.
Levene and Bohak (2012), ‘A Babylonian Jewish Aramaic Incantation Bowl with a List of Deities and Toponyms.’

events.details: Named by the British Museum as previous owner / unclaimed item.
